ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Sitting Bull Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: Establishing care at the clinic for chronic pain in the left ankle and hindfoot with a limp after an old gunshot wound: a culturally safe, trauma-informed history, X-rays, screening for diabetes, high blood pressure and depression, and food. Concerns: He wants to walk his land and ride without pain, and does not want his foot cut open unless there is no other way; He wants care that respects who he is and his own ways of healing; His family does not have enough food at the end of the month. [S]

tr.td: Weight-bearing X-rays of the left foot and ankle: narrowing and bone spurs of the posterior subtalar and talonavicular joints, an old healed irregularity of the plantar heel, a normal ankle (tibiotalar) joint, and several small metallic densities in the soft tissue of the heel

CT of the left foot without contrast: post-traumatic arthritis of the posterior subtalar and talonavicular joints with subchondral cysts; ankle joint preserved; four small metal fragments, the largest 3 mm, in the plantar soft tissue of the heel, none within a joint or bone; no sign of bone infection
Ultrasound-guided injection of the left posterior subtalar joint with triamcinolone 40 mg and lidocaine 1% 2 mL, after consent; pain fell from 6 to 1 of 10 on walking within 15 minutes
Advance care planning conversation, about 20 minutes, with the interpreter

list.item: Hunkpapa Lakota; a respected leader and holy man of his people; lives with his family in a log house on the Grand River near where he was born, on the Standing Rock Reservation, about an hour's drive from the clinic; keeps horses and a garden [S]
Speaks Lakota as his first language and some English; chose to have the clinic's Lakota-speaking interpreter at his visits; asked to be called Sitting Bull [S]

His people's way of life was taken from them within his lifetime: the buffalo are gone, the bands were pursued and exiled, he was held as a prisoner, and his people now farm and depend on government food; he spoke of these losses plainly and chose not to discuss them further at the first visit [S]
Diet: commodity foods (flour, canned meat, lard, sugar, coffee), garden vegetables in season and game when it can be found; food runs short at the end of each month [S]
Does not drink alcohol; does not use commercial tobacco (traditional and ceremonial use was not asked about and is not recorded) [S]

Traditional healing: he has his own spiritual practices and healers and will decide whether and how they are part of his care; the clinic offered access through its traditional medicine program and asked nothing further [S]

Strengths and supports: his standing and responsibilities among his people, a deep spiritual life, decades of endurance, family around him, horsemanship, and a clear sense of what he wants from care [S]

tr.td: Establishing care at the clinic for chronic pain in the left ankle and hindfoot with a limp after an old gunshot wound: a culturally safe, trauma-informed history, X-rays, screening for diabetes, high blood pressure and depression, and food
One-week review, seen the same day by orthopaedic foot and ankle surgery: CT, the diagnosis, retained fragments and lead, and the treatment options
Five-week review: the brace, physical therapy, pain treatment and a subtalar injection
Ten-week review after the injection: pain, function, surgery discussed and declined for now
Sixteen-week review: pain, prediabetes, food and his plan for the year
Same-day sick visit for dyspepsia on naproxen

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Culturally safe, trauma-informed care: ask how he wishes to be addressed and what matters to him, offer the Lakota interpreter, take time, explain each examination and ask consent first, and do not probe his history or beliefs beyond what he chooses to share
Orthopaedic foot and ankle consultation at the clinic's visiting specialist session to confirm the diagnosis and explain every treatment option, including surgery

Imaging: weight-bearing X-rays today; CT if they show arthritis or metal, to map the joints and any fragments; blood lead only if fragments are found, since fragments in a joint or bone raise lead levels

Pain: diclofenac gel first; an oral NSAID for a limited time only after home blood pressure and kidney function are checked; acetaminophen if needed; no opioids, which the Indian Health Service advises against as an initial treatment for chronic pain
A rigid ankle-foot orthosis that holds the hindfoot, a rocker-sole shoe for the other days, a cane in the right hand, and six weeks of physical therapy with a home exercise program
Ultrasound-guided corticosteroid injection of the subtalar joint if pain stays above 4 of 10 after four to six weeks; no more than three or four a year

Surgery (subtalar or double arthrodesis) explained with shared decision-making: what it can and cannot do, months of recovery and the effect on riding; the choice is his, and it is offered again if pain stops him walking or riding

Prediabetes: walking and riding as the foot allows, fewer refined foods and more vegetables and traditional foods, the clinic's diabetes prevention program funded by the Special Diabetes Program for Indians, and hemoglobin A1c again in three to four months
Blood pressure: home readings twice daily for a week with a clinic monitor before the next visit, since one raised clinic reading does not make a diagnosis

Emotional well-being: depression screening with the PHQ-2 and PHQ-9; grief and anger about real losses are not treated as a disorder; behavioral health and traditional healing are available whenever he chooses, side by side with clinic care
Food: the Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations (which offers bison and other traditional foods) or SNAP, garden support, and the Community Health Representative to help with forms
Getting to care: rides from the Community Health Representative program and physical therapy by video on the weeks he cannot travel
Walk a mile on uneven ground and ride with pain of 3 or less
Pain 7 to 3 of 10 on walking; walking more than a mile with the brace; riding again
Decide about surgery with full information, in his own time
Arthrodesis explained with its risks and recovery; he chose to wait and will raise it again if needed
6.0 to 5.8%, with more walking, less flour, lard and sugar, and more garden vegetables and bison
Enrolled in the Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations, including bison and other traditional foods, and a larger garden

list.item: Independent in daily activities; walks with a limp, about half a mile before he must stop; mounts and rides a horse with difficulty; avoids uneven ground [S]

Alert, composed and dignified; watchful at first, then warm; speech measured, through the interpreter and in English; mood steady, tired from broken sleep because of pain; grief and anger about the losses of his people expressed as understandable responses to real events; no thoughts of suicide or of harming anyone [S]
